flagship.title: Medoc Mountain, without a summit campaign
flagship.standfirst: An orange-blazed woodland loop above Little Fishing Creek: a modest walk, a picnic if the day allows, and plenty of time for Rupert to investigate.
flagship.why_this_week: The name promises a mountain; the better invitation is a small woodland circuit. The official Bluff Loop is 1.75 miles and rated easy to moderate, not a strenuous summit expedition. Follow its orange triangles from the signed day-use trail network, allowing time for access walking and unhurried sniffing. This is a new eastern option after last week’s Sandhills and Uwharrie outings. The drive is substantial for a short walk, so make it an easy-paced day rather than a mileage errand. Wet leaves can conceal roots and uneven slopes; Little Fishing Creek is scenery, not an invitation for Rupert to swim. This morning’s dated NWS forecast favours Sunday: mostly sunny near 69F, versus a slight chance of Saturday showers before 1 p.m. Recheck before the drive; a forecast is not a trail inspection.

route.surface: Natural woodland path; orange-triangle blazes. Official difficulty is easy to moderate.

access.name: Medoc Mountain public park access, Hollister
access.parking: Use signed day-use/picnic parking for Bluff Loop, following the official map; the published public park GPS is an access reference, not an assertion of the exact trailhead. The park warns that 1541 Medoc State Park Road can route Google Maps to a closed road: search Medoc Mountain State Park or use 1540 for visitor-center directions, then follow park signs. Do not enter a closed road or use campground parking for this walk. November park hours 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; finish in daylight. Free day use.

panels.label: Follow the orange triangles
panels.text: The named Bluff Loop is 1.75 miles, officially easy to moderate and hiking only. Use the official map at junctions; the three-mile Summit Loop is a different outing.

panels.label: Leave room for pauses
panels.text: Allow roughly 1¼–2 hours with sniffing and access walking. A picnic can round out the day, but turn back for unsafe footing or weather; do not add a harder loop to justify the drive.

artwork.brief: Minimal action mode, following actual latest-six review: four older plates are olive standing profile, cream frontal rest, ochre ball close-up and burgundy frontal walk; the latest two add seated layered autumn woodland and side-on waterside rest. Recent modes are now mixed, so a deliberate minimal action print is appropriate. Choose Rupert in a playful forelegs-down stretch, rear three-quarter side view, head turned gently toward the viewer, on a navy field with a single ochre leaf. Full athletic body and slender tapered tail, fine cream engraving, mustard collar. Distinct dynamic diagonal silhouette, low head/high haunches, sparse ground line and generous upper negative space replace the recent upright/seated/reclining poses; no river, mountain, sun or forest backdrop. Preserve Plate006 likeness and print execution. This is an independent Rupert character moment, not a depiction of the recommended outing.

conditions.trail_note: Follow Bluff Loop’s orange triangles and use the map at junctions. Wet leaves can hide roots and uneven slopes; turn back at flooding, fallen trees or unsafe footing rather than bypassing them. Do not wade or let Rupert swim in Little Fishing Creek. Finish in daylight.

practical.best_window: Sunday morning in full daylight is the first choice in the publication-day forecast. Saturday has a slight shower chance before 1 p.m.; check rain and footing before committing to the drive. Park opens 8 a.m., closes 6 p.m.; finish well before dark.
